cases.title: GHL's rate limit
cases.ghl: GHL limits how fast an app may call it, and answers 429 when the calls come too fast.
cases.fernway: Fernway's queue sends at most 40 requests every 10 seconds, whatever arrives at once. If GHL still answers 429, the lead waits for its next try on the retry clock (case 02). It is never dropped.

proofs.name: waits and tries again when GHL says too many requests
too many requests: waits 30 s sped up 10 times, then delivers

cases.title: Busy, down or silent
cases.ghl: GHL answers 408, 429 or a 5xx error, or says nothing at all for 10 seconds.
cases.fernway: Those pass on their own, so the lead is tried again on the retry clock: 8 tries over about 24 hours. After the eighth it is returned with every answer kept, and one press sends it again.

proofs.name: spreads them over about 24 hours
tries 8 times over 24 h on the promised schedule, then returns the waybill
retries through the queue on its own until GHL takes the lead
no answer, and an expired token: each retried once, then delivered

cases.title: A refusal that waiting won't fix
cases.ghl: GHL refuses the data itself, like a phone number without its country code (any other 4xx).
cases.fernway: Trying again would only repeat the refusal, so the lead is held at once, with GHL's reason in words on its receipt. Once the data is fixed, a resend starts it on a fresh set of tries. A lead GHL could never match (no email and no phone) is refused at the door, before a waybill is made.

proofs.name: holds a lead GHL refuses for its data, at once, with the reason
shows GHL's refusal as words, not JSON
resends a held waybill with a fresh set of tries, on the receipt
runs a resend through the real queue, though its first try's job already ran
refuses a lead GHL couldn't match, with a reason the sender can act on

cases.title: A token running out mid-delivery
cases.ghl: GHL's access tokens expire, and each refresh token can be spent only once.
cases.fernway: Tokens are refreshed 5 minutes before they expire, under a lock, so two workers that need a token at the same moment spend the refresh token once. If GHL answers 401 anyway, Fernway refreshes and tries again. If GHL refuses the refresh, the connection is marked for reconnecting and leads are held with that reason, never lost.

proofs.name: refreshes an expired token once, form-encoded, and keeps the new refresh token
spends the single-use refresh token once even when two workers need a token at the same moment
refreshes the token after a 401 and tries again
marks the connection for reconnecting when GHL refuses the refresh, and holds leads with that reason

cases.title: The same lead, twice
cases.ghl: A website sends a form again after a timeout, or GHL takes a contact but its answer never arrives.
cases.fernway: Each lead carries an idempotency key, so the same lead sent twice is one waybill. Fernway keeps every id GHL gives back (contact, note, meeting, opportunity), so a retry carries on where the last try stopped and never makes a second. Contacts go through GHL's upsert, matched by email, then phone.

proofs.name: makes one shipment of the same lead sent twice
never makes a second contact: a try after a failed stage reuses the contact GHL already gave
never makes a second contact when GHL took the lead but its answer was lost
adds the message once, between the contact and the opportunity, and never again on a retry
books the meeting between the contact and the opportunity, once, even when a later step is retried

cases.title: A crash in the middle
cases.ghl: Not GHL this time: the worker restarts, or the queue loses a job.
cases.fernway: Every scan is written in the same database transaction that moves the lead on, and the app's own database role can add scans but never change or remove one. Every minute a sweep puts back on the queue any lead whose try is more than 2 minutes late. A try that already ran, or isn't due yet, does nothing, so a job that arrives twice is harmless.

proofs.name: lets the app add scans but never change or remove one
puts overdue shipments back on the queue (the safety net if Redis lost them)
does nothing for a try that already ran or isn't due
